figs.title: Mission profile and weight fractions
figs.caption: A sizing mission is a chain of segments, each multiplying the aircraft weight by a fraction: fixed historical values for takeoff, climb, descent and landing, and Breguet exponentials for cruise and loiter. Their product gives W₆/W₀, the fuel fraction adds reserve, and W₀ follows from the iteration with the empty weight fraction.

figs.title: Carrier launch: weight versus end speed
figs.caption: Required catapult end speed grows as √W and shifts down by the wind over deck, while the energy a catapult setting delivers makes its end speed fall as 1/√W. The crossing gives the heaviest launch weight, and more wind over deck moves it to the right.

figs.title: V-n envelope in EAS and true airspeed
figs.caption: Plotted in equivalent airspeed the maneuver envelope is the same at every altitude. In true airspeed the envelope stretches right by 1/√σ, so the corner speed and dive speed are higher true airspeeds at altitude while the load factor limits stay put.

figs.title: Master equation term by term
figs.caption: The master equation is the energy equation divided by βW and V, so each bracket term is a separate demand: parasite drag, induced drag growing with n², climb rate over speed, and acceleration over g. The factor β/α converts the requirement back to sea level static thrust and takeoff weight.
